issues.description: value_to_metric is a near-duplicate of detailed_metric — wrong data shape, not a new feature
issues.detail: Both flags compute the same thing: 'include the entry's runtime value in the metric key segment.' detailed_metric does it for the leaf only, the new flag does it per-level. The right data structure is a single per-descriptor enum/bool that says 'include value at this level', and the leaf descriptor's value of that flag controls the legacy 'detailed' behavior. Instead the PR bolts on a parallel field, a parallel string builder, a parallel walk, and a precedence rule between two flags that mean the same thing. WRONG-DATA-STRUCTURE.

issues.description: Two parallel strings.Builder walks where one labeled segment array would do
issues.detail: GetLimit now maintains detailedMetricFullKey AND valueToMetricFullKey in parallel, plus the original key path implied via rateLimit.FullKey, plus a third reconstruction at the bottom. The data is one sequence of (key, optional value) segments produced by the traversal; render it once at the end based on per-level flags. A []segment with {key, value, includeValue bool} would make the algorithm self-evident and delete most of the branching at lines 343-385. COULD-BE-A-FILTER.

issues.description: The post-loop 'recreate then overwrite' block is dead-weight cleverness
issues.detail: Lines 419-430 call NewRateLimit to 'ensure a clean stats struct' using rateLimit.FullKey, then immediately overwrite Stats and FullKey with the enhanced key. The NewRateLimit call's stats result is discarded one line later. Either the reconstruction matters (then keep it and don't overwrite) or it doesn't (then delete it). As written it's a no-op wrapped in allocation. TOO-CLEVER.

issues.description: Branch structure in the metric-build block collapses to three lines
issues.detail: The if matchedViaWildcard / else if matchedUsingValue / else block at lines 357-385 has three arms that all do the same thing when valueToMetric is true ('append key, then _value if value != ""') and all do the same thing when it's false ('append key'). The matchedViaWildcard and matchedUsingValue distinctions never change the output. The whole block is: write key; if (valueToMetric || matchedUsingValue) && value != "", write _value. Same behavior, ~25 fewer lines, the data flow is obvious. TOO-CLEVER.

issues.description: rateLimitDescriptor struct literal initialization is now positional with four fields
issues.detail: Lines 191 and 268 use positional struct literals: &rateLimitDescriptor{map[string]*rateLimitDescriptor{}, rateLimit, nil, descriptorConfig.ValueToMetric}. Each new field forces every call site to change and silently swaps meanings if order shifts. Named-field initialization costs four tokens and removes a whole class of bug. Small thing; fix it now while you're already touching both call sites.

issues.description: Else branch when nextDescriptor is nil writes a 'deterministic' key that is never read
issues.detail: Lines 386-389 append entry.Key to valueToMetricFullKey when nextDescriptor is nil. When nextDescriptor is nil the loop returns rateLimit on the next iteration condition and the builder result is not used unless a limit was found at a previous level. The comment 'still append something deterministic' admits the author was unsure. Either prove it's load-bearing (test that exercises it) or delete it.

review.summary: The feature is reasonable and the tests are thorough, but the implementation is fighting the data. value_to_metric and detailed_metric express the same idea — 'put the runtime value into this segment of the metric key' — and the PR adds a second flag, a second strings.Builder, a parallel traversal, and a precedence rule rather than unifying them. The metric-build switch on matchedViaWildcard / matchedUsingValue / default produces identical output in all three arms and should collapse to about three lines. The post-loop recreate-then-overwrite block discards the work it just did. Decision: TOO-CLEVER and WRONG-DATA-STRUCTURE — ship the user-visible behavior, but model the metric key as a list of (key, optional value) segments emitted by the walk, render once at the end, and treat detailed_metric as the leaf-only special case of the same mechanism.
